schemes.title: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)
schemes.department: Ministry of Women & Child Development (Mission Shakti)
schemes.brief: Cash help for a pregnant woman or new mother, so she can rest before and after the birth instead of losing wages. For the first child you get Rs.5,000 in two parts, and for a second child you get Rs.6,000 in one go if the baby is a girl. The money goes straight into your Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account. You can apply yourself on the PMMVY portal, or your Anganwadi worker or ASHA can fill the form for you.
schemes.benefit: Rs.5,000 for the first child (Rs.3,000 + Rs.2,000); Rs.6,000 if the second child is a girl
eligibility: Pregnant women and new mothers aged between 18 years 7 months and 55 years when the baby is born

You must fit at least one of these: SC or ST; BPL or NFSA ration card; Ayushman card; e-Shram card; MGNREGA job card; woman farmer getting PM-Kisan; 40% or more disability; family income below Rs.8 lakh a year; pregnant or breastfeeding Anganwadi worker, helper or ASHA
Money is given for the first living child, and for the second child only if it is a girl
You can apply any time from the start of pregnancy up to 270 days after the birth
Not for women in regular government or PSU jobs who get paid maternity leave

Not run in Telangana, which has its own maternity scheme. In Odisha it runs jointly with the state's MAMATA scheme as MAMATA-PMMVY (since April 2025), paying Rs.10,000 for a boy and Rs.12,000 for a girl for up to two births; register at your Anganwadi centre
documents: Aadhaar card of the woman (the husband's Aadhaar is not needed)
Bank or post office account linked to Aadhaar for direct payment (DBT)
Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card with the last period (LMP) date and check-up dates
One eligibility proof: e-Shram card, ration card, job card, Ayushman card, caste certificate, disability certificate or income certificate
Mobile number for OTP and payment messages
For the second part or a second girl child: the baby's birth certificate and vaccination record (14 weeks)

demoFields.label: Login type
demoFields.hint: Press Login at the top right and choose Citizen. Anganwadi and ASHA workers use the other login.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: A number you keep with you. The OTP comes here now, and later the message when money is sent.

demoFields.label: State / District / Block / Village
demoFields.value: Uttar Pradesh / Sitapur / Biswan / Rampur Kalan
demoFields.hint: Where you live now. Your application goes to the Anganwadi centre of this village for checking.

demoFields.label: Beneficiary Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: The pregnant woman's own Aadhaar, not the husband's. Tick the consent box and verify with the Aadhaar OTP.

demoFields.label: Name as per Aadhaar
demoFields.hint: Write the name exactly as printed on Aadhaar, letter by letter, or the payment can fail.

demoFields.label: Eligibility document
demoFields.hint: Pick any one category you belong to, write its number and upload a clear photo of that card.

demoFields.label: LMP date (last period)
demoFields.hint: The first day of your last period, as written on the MCP card by the ANM.

demoFields.label: MCP card registration and ANC date
demoFields.hint: The date your pregnancy was registered and the check-up was done, also on the MCP card.

demoFields.label: Bank account (Aadhaar-based payment)
demoFields.value: Aadhaar-seeded account at Bank of India, Biswan
demoFields.hint: Money is sent to whichever account is linked with your Aadhaar. Ask your bank to link it first if it is not.

demoFields.label: Anganwadi centre
demoFields.hint: Choose the Anganwadi centre near your house. Its worker will visit to confirm your details.

demoSteps: Register your pregnancy at the Anganwadi centre or government health centre, get the MCP card and do the check-up (ANC).
Open pmmvy.wcd.gov.in, press Login, choose Citizen, verify your mobile with OTP and create your profile. If you cannot do it, ask your Anganwadi worker or ASHA to fill the form for you on her app.
Choose Beneficiary Registration, verify Aadhaar with OTP, fill the eligibility proof, LMP and check-up dates and the Anganwadi centre, then submit and note the registration number.
The Anganwadi worker checks your details and the block officer approves. Rs.3,000 is then sent to your Aadhaar-linked account.
After the birth, register the baby's birth and get the 14-week vaccines. Then log in again, or ask the Anganwadi worker, to fill the child's details. Rs.2,000 is sent next.
If your second child is a girl, apply after her birth and 14-week vaccines. Rs.6,000 is sent in one payment.
Check progress under Track Application Status on the portal. For a delay, use Lodge Grievance on the same site or call 1515.

schemes.title: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
schemes.department: National Health Mission, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
schemes.brief: Cash given to a mother who delivers her baby in a government hospital, or in an approved private hospital if she is from a BPL, SC or ST family. The village ASHA helps you register, takes you for check-ups and gets the payment made. Under a separate scheme (JSSK) the delivery itself is free, even a caesarean, along with medicines, food and the ambulance. JSY money is extra, paid into your bank account after the delivery.
schemes.benefit: Rs.1,400 (village) or Rs.1,000 (town) in low-performing states; Rs.700 or Rs.600 elsewhere
eligibility: In Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Assam, Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir: every pregnant woman who delivers in a government hospital or health centre
In all other states: women from BPL, SC or ST families who deliver in a government hospital or health centre
In every state: BPL, SC or ST women who deliver in an approved (accredited) private hospital
There is no age limit and no limit on the number of children for a hospital delivery
BPL women who deliver at home get Rs.500
documents: Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card or JSY card given at registration
Aadhaar card of the mother
Bank account passbook in the mother's name, linked to Aadhaar
BPL ration card, or SC/ST caste certificate (needed outside the low-performing states, and for a private hospital delivery)
Discharge slip or delivery record from the hospital
Mobile number
schemes.submitAt: At the government hospital or health centre where you deliver: before going home, hand your MCP card, Aadhaar copy, bank passbook copy and (where needed) the BPL ration card or caste certificate to the JSY desk or labour-room staff. Your village ASHA can collect and submit them for you. For a home delivery, give them to the ASHA or the ANM at the sub-centre.

demoFields.label: Name of mother
demoFields.hint: The mother's own name, as written on her Aadhaar and bank passbook.

demoFields.label: Husband's name
demoFields.hint: Write it as on the ration card, so the family can be matched.

demoFields.label: Age of mother
demoFields.hint: Your age now. There is no lower or upper limit for a hospital delivery.

demoFields.label: MCP card / RCH ID number
demoFields.hint: The number on your MCP card, given when the ANM registered your pregnancy.

demoFields.label: Category
demoFields.hint: BPL, SC, ST or General. Attach the ration card or caste certificate if you tick BPL, SC or ST.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: The mother's Aadhaar, for checking her identity and for the bank payment.

demoFields.label: Date and place of delivery
demoFields.hint: Filled by the hospital staff from the labour-room register.

demoFields.label: Bank account number and IFSC
demoFields.hint: Copy both from the first page of the passbook. The account must be in the mother's own name.

demoFields.label: Name of ASHA
demoFields.hint: The ASHA who helped you. She is paid separately for helping you.

demoSteps: As soon as you know you are pregnant, tell the village ASHA or go to the sub-centre. The ANM registers you and gives you the MCP card.
Go for the pregnancy check-ups written on the card. Ask for the BPL or caste certificate to be noted if you live outside the low-performing states.
When labour starts, call 102 or 108 for the free ambulance and go to a government hospital or health centre with the MCP card.
Before leaving the hospital, give your Aadhaar, bank passbook copy and MCP card to the JSY desk or labour-room staff, or hand them to the ASHA.
The hospital enters your claim. The money is sent straight to your bank account, usually within a few weeks.
If it has not come in a month, ask the ASHA or the hospital's JSY clerk, or call 104 with your MCP card number.
schemes.helpline: 104 (state health helpline) / 102 (free ambulance for pregnant women) / 108

schemes.title: Ayushman Vay Vandana Card (Ayushman Card for 70+)
schemes.department: National Health Authority, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
schemes.brief: Every person aged 70 or above can get free hospital treatment of up to Rs.5 lakh a year, whatever the family income. It is part of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, and treatment is cashless at any empanelled government or private hospital. If your family already has Ayushman cards, you still get your own extra Rs.5 lakh. You can make the card yourself on the Ayushman website or app with just your Aadhaar.
schemes.benefit: Rs.5 lakh a year cashless treatment for every person aged 70+
eligibility: Every person aged 70 or above, by the year of birth on Aadhaar, rich or poor
If your family already has Ayushman (PM-JAY) cards, you get a separate top-up of up to Rs.5 lakh a year just for yourself
In a new family, husband and wife who are both 70+ share Rs.5 lakh a year between them
People with private health insurance or ESIC can also join
CGHS, ECHS and CAPF members must choose either their own scheme or this one, not both
Available in the states and UTs that run Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
documents: Aadhaar card (the age is taken from Aadhaar, no other age proof needed)
Mobile number for login OTP
Aadhaar-linked mobile for Aadhaar OTP, or face authentication if the mobile is not linked
A live photo, taken on the phone during e-KYC
CGHS, ECHS or CAPF card number, only if you hold one
Present address with PIN code

demoFields.label: Login as
demoFields.hint: Choose Beneficiary. A son or daughter can log in with their own mobile to make the card for a parent.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: Any working number. The login OTP comes here, and the message when the card is ready.

demoFields.label: Enrolment for
demoFields.hint: After logging in, choose the Vay Vandana enrolment option, not the normal family search.

demoFields.label: State
demoFields.hint: The state written in the address on the senior's Aadhaar.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Aadhaar of the person aged 70 or above. Tick the consent box to share Aadhaar details.

demoFields.label: e-KYC method
demoFields.hint: Use Aadhaar OTP if the mobile is linked to Aadhaar. Otherwise scan the face with the Aadhaar FaceRD app.

demoFields.label: Beneficiary category
demoFields.hint: Choose Self declaration, or CGHS, ECHS or CAPF if the senior is in one of these. That choice cannot be changed later.

demoFields.label: Live photo
demoFields.hint: Face straight, good light, no cap or dark glasses.

demoFields.label: Spouse aged 70+
demoFields.hint: Add the husband or wife here only if they are also 70 or above. Their e-KYC is done the same way.

demoFields.label: District and PIN code
demoFields.hint: Where the senior lives now, so nearby empanelled hospitals are shown.

demoSteps: Open beneficiary.nha.gov.in or the Ayushman app and log in as Beneficiary with your mobile number and OTP.
Choose the Ayushman Vay Vandana enrolment option, pick the state and enter the senior's Aadhaar number.
Verify with Aadhaar OTP or face authentication, then take the live photo.
Choose the category, fill the mobile number and address, add the spouse if also 70+, and submit.
Approval usually comes the same day or within a day or two. Log in again and download the Vay Vandana card.
At an empanelled hospital, go to the Ayushman Mitra desk and show the card. Treatment is cashless, so never pay for a covered treatment. You can also get the card made free at that desk.

schemes.title: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
schemes.department: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, with RBI, NABARD and banks
schemes.brief: A cheap farm loan account with a RuPay card, given by banks to farmers for seeds, fertiliser, labour and other farming costs, and also for dairy, poultry, goat rearing and fish farming. Interest is 7% a year, and if you repay on time the government cuts it to 4% on loans up to Rs.3 lakh. No security is needed up to Rs.2 lakh. PM-Kisan farmers can apply with a one-page form at the bank where their PM-Kisan money comes.
schemes.benefit: Farm loan at 4% a year if repaid on time (up to Rs.3 lakh); no security up to Rs.2 lakh
eligibility: Farmers who cultivate land: owners, tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers, and farmer groups (SHG / JLG)
Farmers rearing dairy animals, sheep, goats, pigs or poultry, and fish farmers (inland or sea)
Banks usually lend from age 18 up to 75; above 60 a younger family member joins as co-borrower
The loan limit is fixed by the crop, the land area and the bank's scale of finance
You should not already hold a KCC at another bank
documents: Filled KCC application form with a signature or thumb impression
Aadhaar card
Land record (khatauni, 7/12, jamabandi or patta), or a lease or tenancy paper for tenant farmers
Two passport-size photographs
Bank passbook of the account where PM-Kisan money comes
Details of crops to be grown, or of animals and fish ponds for dairy or fisheries KCC
Details of any existing loan; some banks ask for a no-dues paper from other banks in the area
schemes.submitAt: At the branch of the bank where your PM-Kisan money is credited (or any commercial bank, Regional Rural Bank or cooperative bank branch near your village). Hand the filled form to the field officer or branch manager with your Aadhaar, land record, two photos and passbook, and get the acknowledgement slip at the bottom of the form signed and dated.

demoFields.label: Name of Bank / Branch
demoFields.hint: The bank where your PM-Kisan money comes. Write it at the top of the form.

demoFields.label: Type of KCC
demoFields.hint: Tick fresh KCC for a new card, or enhancement or activation if you already have an old KCC.

demoFields.label: Amount of loan required
demoFields.hint: What you need for one year of farming. The bank will fix the final limit from your land and crops.

demoFields.label: Name of the Applicant
demoFields.hint: Your name as on Aadhaar and the land record.

demoFields.label: Account No (PM Kisan Beneficiary)
demoFields.hint: The account where your PM-Kisan instalments come. The bank takes your KYC from this account.

demoFields.label: Consent for PMSBY / PMJJBY auto debit
demoFields.hint: Insurance of Rs.2 lakh each for Rs.20 and Rs.436 a year, cut from your account. Tick No if you do not want it.

demoFields.label: Details of existing loans
demoFields.hint: Write any loan you have from a bank, cooperative society or other source, with the amount still due.

demoFields.label: Land holding: Village / Survey-Khasra No. / Title / Area
demoFields.hint: Copy from your land record. Tick Leased or Share Cropper if the land is not yours.

demoFields.label: Name of crop to be grown
demoFields.hint: The crops you will sow this year in each season.

demoFields.label: KCC for animal husbandry / fisheries
demoFields.hint: Fill only if you also want a loan for animals or fish farming.

demoSteps: Download the KCC form from pmkisan.gov.in (Download KCC Form) or collect it free at the bank, and fill it.
Take it to your bank branch with Aadhaar, land record, two photos and passbook. Get the acknowledgement at the bottom of the form signed.
The bank officer checks your land record and crops, and may visit the field. The limit is fixed from your crop, land area and needs.
Banks are told to decide within 14 days of a complete application. Sign the loan papers. There is no processing fee for loans up to Rs.3 lakh.
Your KCC account opens and you get a RuPay card. Take out money as you need it, from the branch or an ATM.
Repay within one year, or after harvest, to get the 3% discount, so you pay only 4% interest. The card stays valid for five years with a yearly review.
If the bank refuses or delays without reason, complain to the branch manager in writing, then to RBI on 14448 or cms.rbi.org.in.

schemes.title: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY, farmer pension)
schemes.department: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (run with LIC and CSC)
schemes.brief: A pension of Rs.3,000 a month from age 60 for small and marginal farmers who join between 18 and 40. You pay Rs.55 to Rs.200 a month, depending on your age when you join, and the government adds the same amount. The monthly amount can be cut automatically from your PM-Kisan money. You join at a Common Service Centre (CSC) with your Aadhaar and bank passbook.
schemes.benefit: Rs.3,000 a month pension from age 60; Rs.1,500 family pension to the spouse
eligibility: Small and marginal farmers with up to 2 hectares (about 5 acres) of cultivable land in their own name in the land records
Age 18 to 40 years when joining; you pay every month until you turn 60
Not for people already in NPS, ESIC or EPFO, or who joined PM Shram Yogi Maandhan or PM Vyapari Maandhan
Not for income-tax payers, government or PSU employees (Class IV / Group D staff can join), doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs and architects in practice, or holders of constitutional posts
You need an Aadhaar card and a savings bank account
documents: Aadhaar card
Savings bank passbook or cheque with IFSC (the PM-Kisan account if you want the amount cut from PM-Kisan)
Land record showing land up to 2 hectares in your name
Mobile number
Name and date of birth of your spouse and of the nominee
First month's contribution in cash (Rs.55 to Rs.200)
schemes.submitAt: At your nearest Common Service Centre (CSC). Take your Aadhaar card, bank passbook or cheque, land record and spouse and nominee details, and pay the first month's contribution in cash to the operator (VLE). Joining is free; the enrolment-cum-auto-debit form is printed there for you to sign.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: The operator checks it with your fingerprint, so you must come yourself.

demoFields.label: Name as on Aadhaar
demoFields.hint: Exactly as printed on the Aadhaar card.

demoFields.label: Date of birth as on Aadhaar
demoFields.hint: Your age on this date decides your monthly amount. At 29 it is Rs.100 a month.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: Messages about your contribution and pension come here.

demoFields.label: Bank account number and IFSC
demoFields.hint: Use the account where PM-Kisan money comes if you want the amount cut from it.

demoFields.label: Spouse details
demoFields.hint: Your wife or husband. They get half the pension if you die after 60.

demoFields.label: Nominee details
demoFields.hint: Who gets your savings if you die before the pension starts and your spouse does not continue.

demoFields.label: Land details
demoFields.hint: From your land record. The total must not be more than 2 hectares.

demoFields.label: Pay from PM-Kisan benefit
demoFields.hint: Choose Yes to have the contribution taken from your PM-Kisan instalments, so you never miss a payment.

demoFields.label: Monthly contribution
demoFields.hint: Worked out by the system from your age. You can also choose to pay every 3, 4 or 6 months.

demoSteps: Go to the nearest Common Service Centre with your Aadhaar, bank passbook, land record and spouse and nominee details.
The operator checks your Aadhaar with your fingerprint and fills in your bank, mobile, land, spouse and nominee details. The system shows your monthly amount.
Pay the first month's contribution in cash to the operator.
Sign the enrolment-cum-auto-debit form that is printed. The operator scans and uploads it.
You get your Kisan Pension Account Number (KPAN) and a printed Kisan card on the spot. Keep it safe.
From then on, the amount is cut automatically from your bank account or PM-Kisan money. If you leave within 10 years, you get back your own share with savings bank interest.
At age 60, LIC starts paying Rs.3,000 a month into your bank account. After your death, your spouse gets Rs.1,500 a month.
